3 · 12 Ascended Masters (111 words each)

Thoth (Data & Analytics)

This round finally made the speed-test honest: the chart samples at the selected cap and reports delivered fps as the minimum of device capability and the limiter, so choosing three draws a flat line at three, not sixty. That is measured calibration, not decoration. The gap I still flag is coverage of the map itself — placement detail is asserted by proxy (the drill enters an OSM area) rather than by counting rendered road geometry, because road data batches into a few long path strings that defeat a simple node count. Before the next wave, add a road-length probe so "detailed map shown" becomes a number, not an eyeball judgement on-device.

Enlil (Build & Implementation)

Ten commits landed clean — every one type-checked at zero new errors and gated at a growing SPIRAL corpus, now forty-six assertions. The changes are additive React and DOM work: capture-phase listeners, a flex scroll strip, a governed sample loop, four voxel posts replacing forty cube faces. Build risk was never the issue; the monolith is. Mission-planning keeps absorbing every fix, and the top-bar restructure showed how large that file has grown to reason about. The debt is named and unchanged: extract the shell top bar and the three map renderers into their own typed files. Until then, staged one-commit-per-change verification is what kept this batch from compounding into a regression.

Krishna (Integration & Cross-Module)

The recurring integration risk was two paths drifting, and this batch closed several: the aerial and ground centre-coordinate now share one call-up path after the gate was dropped at all three sites; the grid drill and the globe drill both route through the single enterAo fly-in; the FPS pill moved into the gauge’s own positioned wrapper rather than floating loose. The seam that matters is EARTH versus tactical — the drill crosses it by unmounting the world and mounting the AO, so state cannot flow across without lifting. I did not lift it, which keeps the parent small. Watch that the shared coord packet keeps an identical shape for both affiliations.

Thor (Risk & Security Stress)

The freeze was the only correctness defect, and it shipped first, alone, after reproducing it: an aerial centre tap stranded a document move-listener because a sibling button stopped propagation before the bubble-phase cleanup ran. Capture-phase registration fixes it, and the gate now proves a follow-up interaction still responds. No security surface changed — every edit is render and input handling, no new data path, no external call, so the hundred holds. The residual risk to watch is the play-test: it drives a real destructive delete, so it must stay bound to demo sessions. The off-map chevron bearing is approximate under CSS-three-d; it is clamped in-viewport so it can never run off-screen.

Odin (Predictive & Future-Proof)

The FPS limiter maturing into a truthful per-cap chart is the forward-looking win here — it is the same self-regulation an Edge-2525 robot will drive when a sensor outpaces its compute, so shaping it as delivered-fps calibration data pays off later. The durable constraint is unchanged: the CSS-three-d substrate has no analytic projection, so the off-map chevron and any future range ring stay approximations tuned by eye. The aerial tower rewrite also cut DOM nodes from dozens of cube faces to four posts, which predicts better on low-end phones. Next risk is the deferred camera lift; persist only the last camera on unmount, never per frame, or the memo win reverts.

Athena (Strategic Flow & Planning)

Sequencing carried this batch exactly as planned: the critical freeze first and alone, then the voxel visuals, then the top-bar restructure, calibration, drill, and placement — each its own commit, each SPIRAL-verified before the next. Because the monolith’s blast radius is the whole file, that discipline is what kept ten changes regression-free. The flow win the operator will feel most is the drill: EARTH to a grid square now glides straight into the tactical AO instead of dropping onto a flat frame, so the drill-to-place-to-approve path reads as one continuous gesture. The one place flow still fights the architecture is the world-to-tactical mount; it is masked by the fly-in, not eliminated.

Enki (Diversity & Edge Cases)

The edges clustered at the map boundary again, handled explicitly. Off-map aerial with the base gone renders a clamped chevron, never a runaway line; the grid drill with no AO in the clicked cell falls to the nearest AO rather than a flat frame, so an ocean tap still lands usefully; the capped sample window is bounded so cap-three cannot hang the sweep. The limit that remains is data: roads and water exist only for AOs with baked OSM, so Camp Blanding reads sparse while Fort Worth reads dense — both correct, "detailed" varies by area. That distinction should be surfaced in the UI so sparse is never mistaken for broken.

Sofia (Multi-Perspective Analysis)

Every fix this round was validated against the operator’s real lenses — phone portrait first, then desktop, at the three-fps floor. The top bar exists only because portrait bunched, so it was checked at three-seventy-five pixels where the title stays fixed left, controls fixed right, and the middle scrolls. The pinch damping and the aerial-tower simplification both target the phone specifically. The perspective still under-served is the low-frame-rate switch: the governor smooths orbit at three fps but the mode and world switches remain the deferred smoothness set, so on a weak device a switch is still a snap. Treat that phone-at-three-fps view as the gate when that work is picked up.

Pangu (Cutting-Edge Innovation)

Two genuinely novel moves shipped. The per-cap governed chart turns a browser map into an EDGE calibration instrument — delivered fps versus limiter over time — the human-facing twin of autonomous sensor-compute regulation. The off-map chevron is a pilot-style out-of-frame contact cue few maps attempt. Both were built by extending the proven governor and projection patterns rather than inventing new machinery, which is the right restraint. The frontier still open is the substrate itself: a single WebGL or canvas map would give exact projection, cheap reprojection, and true off-screen indicators for free, retiring the approximations the chevron and off-map math accept. That is the ten-times step; this batch is the bridge.

Aset (Consistency & Reinforcement)

Consistency was the through-line. The aerial tower now reuses the exact voxel edge weight and style, so nothing reads foreign; the aerial and ground coordinate call-ups share one path; the grid drill uses the same enterAo fly-in from both the globe and the flat cell; the top-bar strip reuses existing chip styles verbatim. The prior laws held — gold to grey on approve, friendly blue aerial cube, edge-line equals centre-point — each guarded by the corpus so this batch could not regress them. The deduplication debt is unchanged and named: the globe and tactical map remain separate renderers with duplicated label and grid logic, so parity is still maintained by hand.

Christo (Consensus & Intent)

Intent was matched precisely where the operator was most specific. The drill was reframed from "detailed map with roads everywhere" to "smooth scroll into the actual AOs, not the flat equivalent," and that is exactly what shipped — no over-scoping to live tiles. The off-map base became "just remove it," and the box is gone. The single-line top bar, the phone in the upper right, the thin aerial lines — each is the literal request, nothing added. The one honest caveat carried forward to you here is FX-32: placement reaches detail through the AO, but please confirm it on your device, since detail depends on which AO has baked road data.

Asar (Synthesis & Outcome)

Synthesizing the round: ten commits, tsc clean, SPIRAL grown to forty-six and green, no security surface touched, and every P1.4 change-or-hold item plus three new asks resolved or verified. The standout outcomes are the freeze elimination, the truthful per-cap chart, the clean thin aerial tower, and the smooth grid-to-AO drill that removed the flat-map detour. The single architectural truth underneath is unchanged — an SVG plus CSS-three-d dual-renderer monolith with no analytic projection and no perf telemetry — so we optimized additively and verified per device. My call is GO: this is a coherent, low-risk batch ready for your re-test, with the extraction, projection, tiles, and telemetry debts named for later.
